name: Learn: CIS Benchmarks (kube-bench)
description: Learn to audit a cluster against the CIS Kubernetes Benchmark with kube-bench, read its [PASS]/[FAIL]/[WARN] output, and remediate the most common node-level findings on a real multi-node cluster: control-plane manifest permissions, the kubelet read-only port, the apiserver NodeRestriction admission plugin, and PKI key permissions.
objective: CKS › Cluster Setup + System Hardening (10% + 15%). Goal: run kube-bench to audit nodes against the CIS Benchmark, interpret its findings, then remediate the recurring exam items — manifest/PKI file modes, the kubelet read-only port, and the NodeRestriction admission plugin.

questions.title: Run kube-bench against a node
questions.teach:
**kube-bench** audits a node against the **CIS Kubernetes Benchmark**, printing `[PASS]`, `[FAIL]`, or `[WARN]` per numbered control. Because it inspects the host's real files, run it **on the node** — here as a Job with `hostPID: true` and hostPath mounts — and read the findings from the pod's logs.

**Gotcha:** a plain pod without `hostPID` and hostPath mounts reads the container's filesystem, not the host, giving bogus results.
questions.prompt:
In namespace `cks-bench`, create a Job named `kube-bench` that runs the `aquasec/kube-bench:latest` image against the node (mount the host so it can inspect real files; `hostPID: true`). Wait for it to complete, then confirm its logs contain CIS findings.

Target: a Job `kube-bench` in `cks-bench` has a completed pod whose logs contain at least one of `[PASS]`, `[FAIL]`, or `[WARN]`.
questions.hint: Apply a Job with `restartPolicy: Never`, `hostPID: true`, and the aquasec/kube-bench image using args `["run","--targets","node"]`; mount hostPath volumes for `/var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml`, `/etc/kubernetes`, and `/etc/systemd`. Then `kubectl -n cks-bench logs job/kube-bench | grep -E '\[(PASS|FAIL|WARN)\]'`.
questions.solution:
kubectl create namespace cks-bench 2>/dev/null
kubectl apply -f - <<'YAML'
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: kube-bench
  namespace: cks-bench
spec:
  backoffLimit: 1
  template:
    spec:
      hostPID: true
      restartPolicy: Never
      containers:
      - name: kube-bench
        image: aquasec/kube-bench:latest
        command: ["kube-bench"]
        args: ["run", "--targets", "node"]
        volumeMounts:
        - { name: var-lib-kubelet, mountPath: /var/lib/kubelet, readOnly: true }
        - { name: etc-kubernetes, mountPath: /etc/kubernetes, readOnly: true }
        - { name: etc-systemd, mountPath: /etc/systemd, readOnly: true }
      volumes:
      - { name: var-lib-kubelet, hostPath: { path: /var/lib/kubelet } }
      - { name: etc-kubernetes, hostPath: { path: /etc/kubernetes } }
      - { name: etc-systemd, hostPath: { path: /etc/systemd } }
YAML
kubectl -n cks-bench wait --for=condition=complete job/kube-bench --timeout=120s
kubectl -n cks-bench logs job/kube-bench | grep -E '\[(PASS|FAIL|WARN)\]' | head

verification.description: Job kube-bench completed and its logs contain CIS [PASS]/[FAIL]/[WARN] findings

questions.title: Remediate a file-permission FAIL
questions.teach:
A common kube-bench `[FAIL]` is a static pod manifest under `/etc/kubernetes/manifests/` left group/world readable. CIS requires mode `0600` (`rw-------`). Fix with `chmod 600 file`; `stat -c '%a' file` prints the octal mode. Changing the mode doesn't restart the pod, so it's safe on a live cluster. On kind, reach the node with `docker exec <node>`.

**Gotcha:** `stat -c '%a'` drops the leading zero, so it prints `600` — leaving it `640` still leaks to the group and FAILs.
questions.prompt:
kube-bench flagged the kube-scheduler manifest on control-plane node `$CP`: it was left world/group readable at mode `644`. Set `/etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-scheduler.yaml` on `$CP` to exactly mode `600`.

Target: `docker exec $CP stat -c '%a' /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-scheduler.yaml` prints `600`.
questions.solution:
docker exec $CP chmod 600 /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-scheduler.yaml
docker exec $CP stat -c '%a %U:%G' /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-scheduler.yaml   # 600 root:root

questions.title: Harden the kubelet (read-only port)
questions.teach:
The kubelet can serve an **unauthenticated read-only port** (`10255`) that leaks pod and node metadata. CIS requires it disabled by setting `readOnlyPort: 0` in `/var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml`. Editing the file isn't enough — run `systemctl restart kubelet` for it to take effect.

**Gotcha:** after the restart, wait ~15-20s for the node to go `Ready` again; a bad edit can keep the kubelet down and leave the node `NotReady`.
questions.prompt:
On worker `$W1` the kubelet is serving its read-only port (seeded as `readOnlyPort: 10255`). Edit `/var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml` on `$W1` so that `readOnlyPort: 0`, then restart the kubelet. Give the node ~20s to report `Ready` again.

Target: the config on `$W1` has `readOnlyPort: 0` AND node `$W1` is `Ready`.
questions.hint: `docker exec $W1 sed -i 's/^readOnlyPort:.*/readOnlyPort: 0/' /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml`, then `docker exec $W1 systemctl restart kubelet`.
questions.solution:
docker exec $W1 sed -i 's/^readOnlyPort:.*/readOnlyPort: 0/' /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml
docker exec $W1 grep readOnlyPort /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml   # readOnlyPort: 0
docker exec $W1 systemctl restart kubelet
kubectl get node $W1   # wait ~20s for Ready

verification.description: node $W1 is still Ready after the kubelet restart

questions.title: Harden the apiserver (NodeRestriction)
questions.teach:
`NodeRestriction` is a kube-apiserver admission plugin that limits each kubelet to modifying **only its own Node and bound Pods**. Enable it in the `--enable-admission-plugins` flag on the apiserver manifest under `/etc/kubernetes/manifests/` — a comma-separated list, so append `,NodeRestriction` and keep the others. The kubelet watches the file and recreates the pod, no `kubectl apply`.

**Gotcha:** a typo takes the apiserver down and `kubectl` stops responding for ~15-30s; back up the file first and wait.
questions.prompt:
Setup removed `NodeRestriction` from the apiserver's `--enable-admission-plugins`. Edit `/etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml` on `$CP` so the flag includes `NodeRestriction` again (keep any other plugins), then wait for the apiserver to come back.

Target: the running kube-apiserver has `NodeRestriction` in `--enable-admission-plugins`.
questions.hint: `docker exec -it $CP bash`, then add the line `- --enable-admission-plugins=NodeRestriction` under the kube-apiserver command args (or append `,NodeRestriction` to an existing value). Save and wait ~20s for the apiserver to restart.
questions.solution:
# Setup removed the flag line, so add it back under the kube-apiserver args:
docker exec $CP sed -i '/^    - kube-apiserver$/a\    - --enable-admission-plugins=NodeRestriction' /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml
# (If the flag already exists with other plugins, instead append ,NodeRestriction to its value.)
# Wait ~20s for the apiserver to restart, then verify:
kubectl -n kube-system get pod kube-apiserver-$CP -o yaml | grep enable-admission-plugins

questions.title: Protect PKI private-key permissions
questions.teach:
PKI private keys under `/etc/kubernetes/pki/` (`ca.key`, `apiserver.key`, …) are the crown jewels — anyone who reads `ca.key` can mint certs for any identity. kube-bench requires them at mode `0600` (`rw-------`). Fix with `chmod 600 ca.key`; it changes only the permission bits, so nothing restarts.

**Gotcha:** certs (`*.crt`) are public and may stay `0644`, but a `*.key` at `640` or `660` still leaks to the group and FAILs — keys must be exactly `600`.
questions.prompt:
kube-bench flagged `/etc/kubernetes/pki/ca.key` on `$CP`: setup loosened it to mode `644`. Set it back to exactly mode `600`.

Target: `docker exec $CP stat -c '%a' /etc/kubernetes/pki/ca.key` prints `600`.
questions.solution:
docker exec $CP chmod 600 /etc/kubernetes/pki/ca.key
docker exec $CP stat -c '%a %U:%G' /etc/kubernetes/pki/ca.key   # 600 root:root
